item.title: Katy Perry Condemns Trump Administration’s Use of ‘Firework’ in Military Strikes Video
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our show, where we dive into the latest music news. Today, we're talking about Katy Perry and her recent statement about the use of her hit song "Firework" by the White House.
[Short music transition]
Host: On Saturday, July 25th, Perry took to social media to express her disappointment and anger after the White House used "Firework" in a TikTok post without her permission. The post featured black-and-white footage of military strikes, set to the song's "boom, boom, boom" lyrics. Perry made it clear that she did not approve of this use and does not condone it.
[Short pause]
Host: Perry wrote that she originally intended "Firework" to be an anthem of hope, healing, and inner strength, and she's upset to see it used to promote destruction and violence. She emphasized that her music is meant to bring people together, not celebrate warfare.
[Short music transition]
Host: This isn't an isolated incident. Perry joins a list of artists, including Ariana Grande and Kesha, who have criticized the Trump administration for using their music without permission in political videos and campaign rallies.
[Short pause]
Host: "Firework" was released in 2010 as part of Perry's album Teenage Dream, and it became a huge hit, spending four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100.
[Outro music starts]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you in the next episode.
